context:
Goal: on the iPhone, you can type an Orphaned note, switch tabs, and come back to the same draft.
Problem (goal): with the form's keyboard up, the keys cover the tab bar, and nothing on the Orphaned screen hides them: no drag, no tap, no toolbar. Only Save or Cancel get out, so you can't switch tabs mid-draft, and the test for it (testComposerDraftSurvivesAViewChange) stays red on main.
Based on (read): ux-house-rules-govern L2 says the envelope draft survives a view change.
Based on (read): on main, OrphanedView.swift:279 puts the keyboard up when the form opens and nothing takes it down; HandScreen.swift:144 is the only drag-to-hide in the app.
Departs from: main has no way to hide the keys in the Orphaned form — adds a drag on the Orphaned list that hides them, the same one Card in Hand uses.
Meanwhile: lane pro-ui-main-reds works on the other reds; no merge waits on this.

options.gain: You can reach the tabs mid-draft and keep the draft, and the test goes green.
options.how: The Orphaned list gets the same drag-to-hide as Card in Hand. The test drags first, then switches tabs.
options.label: Add a drag on the list that hides the keys
options.lose: A change to the app: one builder, one reviewer and one Mac run.

options.how: No change to the app. The test stays red under a debt.
options.label: Leave it as it is
options.lose: You can't switch tabs while typing an Orphaned note, and main's iPhone UI run keeps a red.

options.how: Only the test changes: it presses Return to leave the field, once someone reads what Return does to the keys.
options.label: Point the test at the Return key instead
options.lose: Return also adds the typed name (OrphanedView.swift:199), so it may not be how you switch tabs, and the keys may still stay up.

ref: step pro-ui-main-reds (the iPhone UI test reds on main); decision ux-house-rules-govern (L2: the envelope draft survives a view change); test testComposerDraftSurvivesAViewChange
title: On the iPhone, the keyboard in the Orphaned note form covers the tabs, and nothing hides it. Add a drag that hides the keys?
why: It gives you the tab switch the ruling promises, with a drag the app already uses on Card in Hand.
